claims.claim: Aeva's FMCW 4D LiDAR links perception technology to autonomous trucking and heavy-vehicle active safety, where long-range sensing supports safer machine navigation.

The same photonics platform is being extended toward industrial sensing and optical connectivity, creating cross-market optionality but moving the successor bottleneck from sensing performance toward scaled production, qualification and customer conversion.

causalEdges: 4D LiDAR capability -> reliable long-range perception -> autonomous/active-safety systems -> safer freight mobility
photonics platform reuse -> optical-connectivity/industrial opportunities -> broader infrastructure relevance
pre-series awards -> production qualification and volume conversion -> recurring economics
falsifiers: Major vehicle programs fail to convert from samples/development into series production.
Competing sensing stacks deliver adequate safety/performance at lower system cost, weakening Aeva's bottleneck position.
unknowns: unit economics and committed volumes across awards
timing to material positive cash generation

claims.claim: Broad design-win momentum does not yet establish scaled economics; the $115M follow-on strengthens liquidity while confirming ongoing external-capital dependence.
Exclusive or selected development positions reduce technical adoption uncertainty but do not remove customer concentration, program timing, substitution or dilution risk.

contradictions.contradiction: Commercial-design-win momentum is broadening faster than disclosed scaled production economics are becoming visible.

unknowns: unit economics and committed volumes across awards
timing to material positive cash generation
